messages:
Mira: Heads-up — we just saw a Dedicated customer hit inference errors after the latest quant-profile rollout. stack traces point to a profile parsing mismatch when we read cached profiles from S3/local cache.
Sam: ugh. do we know which profile version?
Mira: looks like older profiles (generated ~6mo ago) that assume the old header layout. runtime now expects a 3-byte header + schema id. Old ones just had 2 bytes.
Juan: this is exactly why we needed schema versioning :/ Any chance to gracefully handle both?
Cheng: We can. Options: 1) runtime accepts both and normalizes to v2 in memory, 2) background migration job to rewrite profiles in S3/cache, 3) force invalidation and recompute on first use. Tradeoffs: (1) increases runtime parsing complexity, (2) migration is eventual but heavy IO, (3) invalidation causes CPU/regeneration spikes.
Liam: From infra POV, (3) is easiest short-term if we can throttle regen. But we need a compatibility matrix and explicit guarantees for older customers.
Mira: Proposed immediate plan: short-term fallback parsing (+ permissive mode) so we don't crash, emit telemetry, and start a controlled migration job for S3 blobs. Long-term: add schema_version field and signing, and bump on-disk cache format.
Sam: Agree. What does permissive parsing look like? Example: try v2 parse, on failure attempt v1 legacy parse, then normalize. Add a profile checksum and attach a parsed_version tag.
Cheng: sketch of legacy header detector:
```
# pseudo
header = read(4)
if header[0:2]==b'QP' and header[2] in (1,2):
  schema=header[2]
else:
  # legacy: only 'Q' + flags
  schema=1
  rewind and parse legacy fields
```
We can implement as a small adapter module.
Juan: Need to be careful about FP8 vs INT8/4-bit semantics. Some old profiles didn't contain per-attn quant params and assumed global scale. If we silently normalize, quality could change. We must tag normalized profiles and run the eval suite per model+profile after migration.
Mira: Good call. Add migration QA: for each profile rewritten, run a lightweight eval (2-3 prompts) and compare degradation < 0.5% fail-rate. If > threshold, keep original and mark for manual review.
Liam: Ops: for migration job we'll shard by bucket, run at low concurrency, and emit metrics: profiles_migrated, profiles_failed_qcheck, profile_read_fallthroughs. We'll need a k8s job and a replay queue for failed ones.
Sam: Also add runtime guard: if permissive parse produced a normalized profile, increment sampled telemetry that includes model, profile_hash, quant_type (FP8/INT8/4bit), and a small sample of logits diff histogram. Keep sample size tiny (~0.1%).
Mira: Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: deploy permissive parser and telemetry (canary 5% traffic) — 48h watch.
- Phase 1: start S3 migration job for canary customers, run QA checks.
- Phase 2: increase migration scope, invalidate local caches where safe.
- Phase 3: once >95% migrated and QA green, flip strict parser and mark v2 as required.
Juan: What about private deployments? Some customers have their own on-disk caches we cannot rewrite. Need a migration CLI and docs for them to run.
Cheng: We'll add a small `redwood-quant-migrate --source <cache-dir|s3-uri>` tool that performs the same rewrite + QA, and outputs a report. Easy to ship as a tiny static binary.
Liam: Also document rollback: if normalized profile fails QA, we keep both versions and the runtime will prefer the original for that customer until they manually approve migration.
Mira: Action items:
- Sam: implement permissive parser + telemetry hooks (due 3 days).
- Cheng: prototype migrate CLI + QA harness (due 7 days).
- Liam: k8s job + throttling plan + dashboard (due 5 days).
- Juan: write migration QA thresholds and test vectors (due 4 days).
- Mira: draft customer comms and private-deploy docs (due 3 days).
ops-bot: Note: reminder set — follow-up sync in 5 days. :white_check_mark:
Sam: I'll open a short RFC PR summarizing the schema change and include the compatibility matrix for FP8/INT8/4bit (per-layer vs global flags).
Juan: one more: add a gating flag so customers can opt-in to auto-migration for sensitive models.
Mira: agreed. ok team — let's move. I'll post status updates in this thread during rollout. :rocket:
